why: L1.informal-contractions: only 2 of 424 pool items had any; widened past gonna/wanna on 2026-10-29 (Daniel: other casual contractions too).
behaviour: the speaker uses informal spoken contractions, two to four of them, naturally, picked from: gonna, wanna, gotta, hafta, kinda, sorta, lemme, gimme, dunno, 'cause, outta, lotta, oughta, tryna, gotcha, c'mon, 'em, ya (for you), shoulda, coulda, woulda, musta, whaddya, y'know. Keep ordinary contractions (don't, I'm, it's, we'll) as well
rule: Expand informal spoken contractions: gonna -> going to, wanna -> want to (wants to), gotta / hafta -> have to ("I've gotta" -> "I've got to"), kinda -> kind of, sorta -> sort of, lemme -> let me, gimme -> give me, dunno -> don't know ("I dunno" -> "I don't know"), 'cause -> because, outta -> out of, lotta -> lot of, oughta -> ought to, tryna -> trying to, gotcha -> got it, c'mon -> come on, 'em -> them, ya -> you, shoulda / coulda / woulda / musta -> should have / could have / would have / must have, whaddya -> what do you, y'know -> you know (or drop it as filler). Keep ordinary contractions (don't, I'm, it's, we'll) as they are.
